memories.content: Link expected participant burden in each user study task to its corresponding mitigation strategy.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the prototype and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided during user study sessions.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately after collection.
Specify the equipment to be loaned to participants who lack necessary devices.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
HCI ethics reviewers verify that expected burdens and mitigation strategies correspond to each user study task.
Inform participants that the formative evaluation prototype is not a finished service.
Set an upper limit on cumulative task burden when requesting repeated evaluations from the same participant.
The author of this proposal tends to emphasize expected benefits of the prototype over participant burden.
In organizations where leaders or institutional staff handle recruitment, recruitment authority and academic or professional evaluation authority may be combined in the same role.
Allow the problem framing to extend through a third sentence when a concrete person, setting, or use situation is needed to make the issue understandable.
Use the third sentence for the specific setting and consequence rather than compressing them into an abstract two-sentence summary.
Explicitly specify the users, operational stakeholders, and actual usage environment in the primary HCI research question.
Provide one compact visual summary when proposing an unfamiliar interaction procedure.
Mark the conditions that move an unfamiliar interaction procedure from one step to the next in its visual summary.
Present the master’s research schedule as phase-specific milestones for field understanding, system implementation, user study, and analysis.
Link deliverables that determine entry into the next phase to each milestone of the master’s research.
Directly connect the gap in the actual usage context with the proposed design and operational contributions in a single flow.
Avoid extra subheadings in a two-page proposal; use paragraph transitions to preserve one continuous argument from problem to proposed response and next steps.
Begin each paragraph by connecting it to the previous claim so the short proposal reads as an argument rather than a stack of labeled fragments.
Place preliminary results from field observations or technical validations near sentences supporting feasibility claims.
Readers may misinterpret a compressed opening when the person, setting, or consequence is only implied.
A two-sentence opening can become so general that readers understand the topic but cannot picture the situation the proposal intends to change.
Use paragraph transitions instead of extra headings when the repeated labels would consume space needed for the argument itself.
End each paragraph with the question or consequence that the next paragraph answers.
A continuous sequence of problem, consequence, response, and next step makes the relationship among claims audible without repeating section labels.
Readers may experience very short headed sections as an outline because each new label interrupts the connection to the previous paragraph.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate aspects of an HCI proposal. The reference frame concentrates on participant protections, access, equipment, and recruitment power, while the compared frame concentrates on concise proposal framing, argumentative flow, visual explanation, evidence placement, and milestone planning. No shared or contradictory policy is present.

relations.reason: These memories describe the preparation and review steps of one reference-only task-level burden-control claim; the compared frame has no corresponding ethics-review content.
relations.summary: Expected participant burdens and mitigation strategies are linked by study task and checked by ethics reviewers.

relations.reason: These memories split one reference-only accommodation-planning claim into required supports and delivery arrangements; the compared frame does not address participant accommodations.
relations.summary: Necessary accessibility accommodations are identified and their provision during study sessions is specified.

relations.summary: Participant equipment loans specify both the devices provided and the return procedure.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only safeguard for repeat participation with no counterpart in the compared frame.

relations.summary: An unfamiliar interaction procedure receives a compact visual summary that marks the conditions governing movement between steps.

relations.summary: The master’s research schedule uses phase-specific milestones whose deliverables determine entry into subsequent phases.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-only contribution-framing requirement absent from the reference frame.

relations.reason: These memories provide complementary rules and rationales for one compared-only paragraph-continuity strategy; the reference frame contains no corresponding document-structure guidance.
relations.summary: A short proposal uses backward- and forward-linking paragraph transitions instead of space-consuming headings to sustain a continuous problem-to-next-step argument.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame uniquely covers concrete problem framing, contextualized research questions and contributions, visual procedure summaries, phase-gated schedules, continuous paragraph-level argumentation, and placement of preliminary evidence near feasibility claims.
reports.reference_only: The reference uniquely covers task-level burden mitigation and review, accommodations, data de-identification, equipment loans, prototype-status disclosure, cumulative burden, benefit-burden bias, and recruitment conflicts involving evaluative authority.
